current_metrics.methodology_label:
ZCIS rate level for a single (curve_family, tenor) curve pillar
read directly from
``macro_data.instrument_master`` × ``macro_data.v_market_data_daily_enriched``
filtered by ``instrument_type='inflation_swap'`` AND
``pricing_type='zero_coupon_breakeven'`` AND ``curve_family=?``
AND ``tenor=?``.  Returns the current rate, period changes
(daily / weekly / monthly), rolling z-score against the 252-day
window, trailing range stats (high / low / percentile within
the trailing 252 days), the observation count over the user's
lookback_days window, AND the load-bearing reference metadata
``inflation_index_family`` / ``index_lag`` / ``interpolation``
/ ``underlying_index`` so a desk reader can interpret the level
honestly: USD_ZCIS references US_CPI_URBAN with a 3M lag and
daily interpolation; EUR_ZCIS references EU_HICP (ex-tobacco)
with a 3M lag and monthly interpolation; GBP_ZCIS references
UK_RPI with a 2M lag and monthly interpolation — these
conventions are NOT comparable cross-curve without harmonising
them.  Plus the canonical ``time_series`` payload over the
displayed window.

time_series.description: Historical zero-coupon inflation swap (ZCIS) rates for EUR_ZCIS 10Y over the display window (cleaned, ffill'd; rounded to 4 decimals to match current_metrics.zcis_rate_pct exactly at the latest row).  Reference: inflation_index_family='EU_HICP', index_lag='3M', interpolation='Monthly'.  These conventions differ across USD_ZCIS / EUR_ZCIS / GBP_ZCIS — cross-curve comparisons are NOT pure expected-inflation differentials without harmonising them.
